html:
The Ethiopian-Adal war was fought from 1529 to 1543 between the Christian Ethiopian empire and the Muslim Adal Sultanate of Harar, led by Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim, known as Gragn, the left-handed.

After his victory at Shimbra Kure in 1529, Ahmad's armies, using Ottoman firearms, overran most of the highlands, burning churches and monasteries and converting many people. Emperor Lebna Dengel died a fugitive.

A Portuguese force of about 400 musketeers under Cristóvão da Gama, son of Vasco da Gama, came to help. Emperor Galawdewos killed Ahmad in battle at Wayna Daga in 1543. Both sides were exhausted, which let the Oromo migrations move into the highlands and the Muslim lowlands. The war is remembered differently by Christians and Muslims in Ethiopia and Somalia.
sum: The Ethiopian-Adal war was fought from 1529 to 1543 between the Christian Ethiopian empire and the Muslim Adal Sultanate of Harar, led by Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim, known as Gragn, the left-handed.
